recipes.name: Spicy Fish Soup
ingredients_raw: 1 (4 ounce) can canned green chile peppers, chopped
1.5 cups canned peeled and diced tomatoes
0.5 cup medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
0.5 pound cod fillets, cut into chunks

steps.text: Spray a large saucepan with cooking spray and heat over medium-high heat. Add onion and sauté, stirring often, until translucent, about 5 minutes. Add garlic and chili powder; sauté until fragrant, about 2 minutes.
Stir in chicken broth, chile peppers, and cumin; bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add tomatoes, bell pepper, shrimp, and cod; increase the heat to medium and return to a boil. Reduce the heat to low, cover, and simmer for 5 more minutes.
Gradually stir in yogurt until heated through.

raw_recipe.headline: Spicy Fish Soup
raw_recipe.description: This spicy fish soup packed with shrimp, cod, bell peppers, diced tomatoes, cumin, and chili powder is mixed with yogurt for a creamy effect.

review.reviewBody: I happened to have every single ingredient in the house except for the yogurt, but I made it anyway. Oh my goodness, this soup was WONDERFUL! I can guarantee I will be making this soup often. It reminds me of my grandmother, who was from interior Mexico. My cooking this dish would have made her proud! Excellent!

This is definitely going in the "keep" pile.
Even my super picky husband absolutely LOVED it.
I used fresh tomatoes and jalapeños instead of canned stuff and added them with the cumin to cook for the 20 minutes. I also added fresh celery and zucchini with the seafood for the last 5 minutes and topped it all of with sour cream instead of the yogurt. The flavor was amazing and I will be making this again for sure

I didnt see how it says to cook the fish/shrimp so i seasoned the fish (salt, pepper, cayenne, garlic, onion, cumin, chili powder) and cooked in canola oil in a skillet. I doubled the recipe. Used 4 Jalapeno in place of a can of green chiles. Used 2 fresh tomato in place of a can. Chose fire roasted tomato. Used Sour Cream instead of yogurt. Very good, heckin spicy!!

Loved the idea!! I'm in a weight loss plan and this recipe fit in very well! Read all the reviews and modified in the following ways: 1) doubled liquid content; 2) used grilled Hatch Peppers from earlier in the summer; 3) put a dollop of plain yogurt in each bowl rather than adding to the cooking pot, and topped with fresh cilantro; 4) added fresh corn cut off the cob; added a shake of hot-sauce to taste. I love being able to prepare tasty, healthy, flavorful food!

I love this...flavorful and filling. I've made a few changes that work for me but it's great as presented. I spoil myself and use smoked salmon for the meat (making sure I use unsalted broth) and creme fraiche rather then yougurt.

I need a recipe to avoid wasting leftovers from last night's roasted branzino. This worked out great. I had some hatch chiles I had frozen a couple of months ago--amounting to 4 oz, luckily enough. I only lacked a bell pepper and yogurt. I used a full 2 cups of chicken broth, rather than one and a half, rather than save (and waste) 4 oz. It all turned out very well. I liked the spice flavor and level of hotness. I didn't feel a need for hot sauce. I would use more shrimp next time. I suspect "1/2 cup shrimp" is a misprint; that's hardly anything! I added a dollop of sour cream to my first helping. It curdled, but tasted OK. My second helping with anything else added was thoroughly satisfying. I will make this again.

I modified the recipe slightly. I added two small red potatoes (diced) and a can of corn. I also added the green bell pepper before the first boil since I like the flavor of pepper in my soups. My husband had 3 bowls and my neighbor came over to claim the remains! Shouldn't have post it on Facebook if I didn't want to share ;) Everyone loved it! A keeper.

Another hint is that I squeezed lemon in my soup and chopped cilantro on top to garnish and for taste, to truly make it a Mexican dish.

I made this last night for my family and needless to say, it went quick. It was such a hit that I made more and took it to my Mom and brother. Everyone agreed that it was the best fish soup they ever had.

Changes: I didn't add tomatoes since I was out of them, added a tbsp of hot jalapeno green salsa for a nice kick, then at the final stage I added a tbsp of fresh chopped parsley, and 2 tbsp of heavy whipping cream. Since using chicken bouillon can sometimes make a dish saltier, I added 2-1/4 cups of water with 2 chicken cubes.

Just made it -- had my first bowl. OMG, this is extremely tasty and warming. Followed everything. Had homemade chicken stock to use, and added splashes of: fish sauce, tamari, and vinegar. Used sour cream and it is PERFECTION! Thank you so much! 💜❤️💙

Not a bad base, but definitely needs some work. First just skip the yogurt, no one needs that nonsense. Then substitute 1 or 2 large fresh jalapeños for the can of chilis, but then pour in about 1/4 cup of tomatilla salsa for that green chili flavor. Odds are it still won't be very spicy, but whatever that is what hot sauce is for. One & a half cups of broth is clearly inadequate, just fill that pot with a solid quart. I have no idea why anyone would use just 1 clove of garlic, you need at least 3/4 of an entire bulb, a clove is a snack not an ingredient. Oh and add salt, lots of salt.

Excellent recipe. I doubled it and subbed 1c light sour cream and 1/2c Greek yogurt instead of all yogurt. Also one 4oz can of chopped jalapeno for the chopped green chilies. I sprinkled a little cayenne with the chili powder. We really enjoyed it.

Edit: I made this again and had a problem with curdling when I added the yogurt. Next time I will use all light sour cream.
I didn’t have yogurt so I used heavy whipping cream. My family really liked it. Even my picky eater liked it. We like spicy food. Next time I will add a bit more chile powder.
I have cooked this 10 times in a few months. I have to say I Triple the fish and shrimp, add potatoes, and dont use the yogurt. I absolutely love this and my family loves this

I've been making this recipe for 7 years now. Loved by everyone. I don't like it too spicy so I usually leave out most of the chili powder and increase the amount of cumin. I also use sour cream instead of yogurt in lesser amount too!
I have made it at least once a month over the past year. Very flavorful.

Quick, tasty dish. I usually work with what's on hand so used tilapia (no shrimp) and really enjoyed the result. I did add a couple of splashes of fish sauce and red wine vinegar to boost the umami. And a dash of soy sauce. Will make this again soon. * And as others have mentioned, I didn't include the yogurt.

As others suggested, I did not use yogurt and increased the garlic. It was tasty and intense and the kind of thing that would be great to have if you're sick. 1.5 cups of chicken broth however is a recipe for fish stew or something you would pour over rice. If you want to make soup, you have to double the amount of broth. This recipe contained adequate heat and I did not feel the need to add more hot sauce, and the chicken broth meant that for me no additional salt was required, although I suppose one could have done so. I wonder what this recipe would be like with vegetable broth instead of chicken broth.

In the words of Guy Fieri: "Holy Salami, Call my Mommy!"...this was FANTASTIC! I did take one readers advice and bought the diced tomatoes with the green chilis in it. I prefer a tomato-based broth, so I reduced the chicken broth by 1/2cup and added 3/4 cup of tomato sauce....YUMM-O! I didn't have nonfat yogurt but simply used 3/4 c of fat free sour cream...delicious!!! I also like spicy, so I added 1/2 tsp of red chili flakes. I served it over rice and with crusty bread...one of my new favorites! July 4, 2023 - This dish is still one of our favorite dishes and a very easy to pull together meal. I have since omitted the tomato sauce and just relied on the tomatoes with chilies to give the broth a tomatoey taste. My husband needs a renal diet due to needing a kidney transplant, so the tomato sauce was too acidic. But I now add chopped squash for extra nutrients and color. We LOVE this dish!!

Omg...we smoked a big cod and I didn't know what to do with it. ..I ran across your recipe..what do to with left over cod...made this soup...WOW..so good 👍 take your time and let it simmer like the recipe says..SO GOOD ..thank you..
This was wonderful. I’ll definitely be making this soup often.
